sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Jensen Huang’s $21 billion net worth at stake: CEO’s admission of affair with an alleged Chinese spy is ‘capping gains’ for Nvidia stock
sources.text: For the first time in a long time, Nvidia’s investors may be feeling a little cold about their investment’s performance. Last week, the famed chipmaker and many of its peers in the wider AI and technology industry suffered an estimated $2.5 trillion rout as investors questioned the hurdles facing the sector. The issue is political: The midterms saw Democrats win the Senate, the House, and many statehouses, prompting the question of whether regulation will become more complex under a divided government. But adding to Nvidia investors’ concerns is the admission of its CEO, Jensen Huang, that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang’s net worth, tied to the computer processor and AI company he co-founded, stood at just over $171 billion early last week. It dropped to $150.9 billion by Thursday, and briefly rebounded to $154.9 billion by Friday—the latest data point on Bloomberg’s Billionaires Index . The trajectory follows the path of Nvidia’s share price, now down 18.6% in the past month. But even as signs of a small reversal bloomed Friday, the weekend brought another blow. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Huang said in a statement shared overnight. “To my colleagues at NVIDIA … you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility,” he added, saying he would work to “earn back” the confidence of the board, partners and company shareholders. The woman he had an affair with has been identified in a series of reports as a suspected Chinese spy. Nvidia’s board of directors confirmed in an accompanying statement overnight that it had launched an independent investigation “in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.” The Chinese government has denied involvement in the alleged spy plot involving Huang, calling the debacle “nothing but smears.” The board added that while it has no reason to believe sensitive national security or NVIDIA “secrets” were compromised, it will “examine all available information.” Analysts are digesting the news this morning ahead of markets opening in New York. Equities in Asia rallied this morning, noted Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid, “although concerns surrounding an internal investigation involving Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang are capping gains.” “The company is down around -3.5% on platforms that provide weekend prices,” he added. The importance of Nvidia among the companies at the forefront of AI development cannot be overstated. It is the premier supplier of chips to AI companies and one of the largest investors and guarantors of companies in the AI supply chain—to the tune of hundreds of billions. Yet President Trump was unruffled when asked about one of the country’s most famous CEOs being potentially implicated in a national security threat. “I have not spoken to [Huang] about it,” Trump told reporters last night. “I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what is going on.” Betting on the prediction market Kalshi had the odds of Huang leaving the company before July 27 at 25%. Professor Jeffrey Sonnenfeld, senior associate dean for leadership studies at the Yale School of Management, put the odds of his resignation at 50-50 . Huang owns the largest single stake in Nvidia , and his children are among his employees. If he were to leave, there is no obvious successor. Nvidia’s board said it has “confidence in Jensen and his leadership team.” President Trump was also confident Huang would continue to lead the company, saying: “He’s done an amazing job for our country.”

sources.title: What is Megaspeed? The Nvidia chip buyer in the spotlight after Jensen Huang’s affair
sources.text: Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed is in the international spotlight after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife, following reports linking him to Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. U.S. intelligence officials believe she is a Chinese intelligence asset, according to The New York Times. While the Nvidia CEO — one of the world's most prominent executives and a figurehead of the AI industry – did not name Megaspeed or Alice Huang in his statement, he acknowledged his infidelity and said Nvidia's Board of Directors had begun an independent investigation "regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports." "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," he said. Nvidia said in a statement it had "no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised," but that its "Board's inquiry will examine all available information." Tech darling Nvidia sells advanced AI and data center chips and has customers including Microsoft , Amazon , Google , Meta and Oracle . The explosion in AI adoption in recent years has fueled its stock and pushed it to a $5 trillion market cap earlier this year. Megaspeed sells services to Asia Pacific-based companies that need large amounts of computing capacity, usually for AI projects, by selling access to computing resources hosted in data centers in Southeast Asia. It advertises itself as a "core business partner" of Nvidia's computing power cloud business in the region, allowing customers to rent computing power from Nvidia GPUs, or "graphics processing units" — specialized chips designed to do many calculations at the same time. The service allows businesses to complete costly AI operations without buying and operating all the hardware themselves. It can also give customers remote access to computing power from advanced chips located outside China. U.S. controls restrict the export of some advanced chips to China, but remote access is a separate question. Megaspeed, which has offices in Singapore and Indonesia, has previously faced media and government scrutiny over whether some of its GPUs have been redirected to China. A report published by Bloomberg in December 2025 stated that the U.S. government was investigating Megaspeed's ownership structure and whether it had smuggled Nvidia chips to China. A response to the article published on Megaspeed's website said it contained "misleading information and incorrect insinuations." It added that inspections by the Bureau of Industry and Security of the U.S. Commerce Department, the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry of Malaysia, and Nvidia had found "no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities." Businesswoman Alice Huang is an "executive" at Megaspeed and a "publicly reported Chinese intelligence asset," according to a House Select Committee on China statement on Nov. 5. Committee heads have requested Jensen Huang's attendance at a Nov. 18 briefing to establish "the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk" after reports raised "significant national security concerns regarding [China's] access to sensitive U.S. technology and information." According to New York Times reporting this month, Alice Huang is a Chinese citizen who speaks good English and is well-connected among high-ranking chip industry executives. The Times reported on Friday that a memo was distributed among policymakers in the Trump administration last spring identifying a Chinese businesswoman with a close relationship to Jensen Huang as passing information about U.S. AI chips to Beijing's top spy agency and seeking policy influence. Bloomberg reports that Alice Huang also goes by Huang Le and helped set Megaspeed up in 2023, shortly after the U.S. issued its first chip export bans targeting China during the Biden administration. The sanctions are an attempt to curb Chinese breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, especially in military applications, via U.S.-made technology. Bloomberg previously listed her as one of the people collaborating with a Singapore police investigation into the company's activities in relation to China. Singapore's government has said it had not investigated Alice Huang's alleged intelligence ties or her relationship with Jensen Huang. CNBC has contacted Megaspeed for comment. The reports about the relationship prompted renewed scrutiny of Jensen Huang's past comments on engaging with the Chinese market. He told CNBC's Arjun Kharpal on Oct. 22: "No market is closed forever, and China wants foreign companies to invest in China, just as Germany wants foreign companies and countries to invest in Germany." "And so the market has to be open and it has to be welcoming. There's no reason to believe that market is going to be closed to the best competitors in the world, and Nvidia is surely the best in the world at doing what we do." Correction: This article has been corrected to change an instance of an incorrect spelling of Jensen Huang's name.

sources.title: 'I am deeply sorry': Jensen Huang affair with suspected Chinese spy sees Nvidia open investigation into its CEO — but what happens next?
sources.text: Nvidia share price drops in early trading following reports of Huang affair Nvidia has opened an internal investigation into its CEO Jensen Huang after he was accused of having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Huang has apologized for his actions in a letter to Nvidia staff, with the company saying it would now look into the incident, but was confident that no internal or national security secrets were compromised. Nvidia shares were down 5% pre-trading on Monday, which might seem small, but it is one of the world's biggest companies, valued at around $4.50 trillion following its key role in powering the AI boom. The Nvidia CEO is suspected of having an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based IT and cloud company currently under investigation for smuggling Nvidia GPUs into China. Suspicion around an extra-marital relationship first arose in 2025, when US intelligence agencies watching Megaspeed and Alice Huang reported her relationship with the Nvidia CEO. The New York Times published an initial report on the affair in November 2026, which Huang had called "groundless speculation", but the CEO was then called to Congress to give a closed-door briefing about the incident. “Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” said Michigan Rep. John Moolenaar, who is also chairman of the House Select Committee on China. Nvidia's board has issued a statement saying it would now begin "an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort." "The Board prioritises US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of Nvidia and its shareholders," it added. "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information. "Jensen fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it." In his statement, Huang, who said he was "fully committed" to Nvidia, confessed, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," he said in a letter to staff. "Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it. "To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust." The question now is what happens to Huang - one of the most visible and central figures of the current AI boom. Nvidia has been transformed from a gaming graphics card provider into one of the world's most important companies in recent years, with Huang's dynamic leadership helping power much of that. This prominence has led him to become a central figure in world debates on technology, with Huang celebrated by President Trump (who has already come out in support of Huang, calling him "a fine person") on several occasions. We have seen leaders and CEOs lose their jobs for far less than this in recent years, so will Nvidia's board be prepared to do the unthinkable and remove the leader which made the company what it is? sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: Como usar o mapa do Gemini para encontrar novos lugares?
sources.text: Por Viviane França • Editado por Jones Oliveira | 07/11/2026 às 14:00 O Google lançou uma nova ferramenta chamada “Mapa” para o aplicativo Gemini em celulares. Com ela, você pode escolher uma região no mapa e pedir à inteligência artificial informações, recomendações e sugestões relacionadas ao local selecionado. A ferramenta é útil para quem quer encontrar restaurantes, pontos turísticos, lojas ou outros lugares de interesse sem precisar informar apenas o nome de uma cidade ou bairro. Ao abrir o recurso, o Gemini mostra um mapa da região atual do celular com uma área circular destacada . Você pode arrastar o mapa, aproximar ou afastar a visualização para posicionar a área sobre o local que deseja pesquisar. Também dá para procurar outro endereço ou região pelo ícone de lupa no canto superior direito. Depois de encontrar o local desejado, toque em “Explorar esta área”. O Gemini adiciona automaticamente a etiqueta “Área do Mapa” à caixa de texto, indicando que a região selecionada fará parte do contexto da conversa. A partir daí, é só fazer a pergunta ou enviar uma instrução, como pedir restaurantes próximos, pontos turísticos ou lugares interessantes para visitar. O recurso “Mapa” já está disponível nos aplicativos Gemini para Android e iOS , mas ainda não chegou à versão web. A ferramenta aparece no menu aberto pelo botão “+”, ao lado de opções Fotos, Câmera, Avatar, Arquivos, Drive e Notebooks. Caso você não queira adicionar uma região à conversa, basta tocar no botão “X” para fechar o mapa. Confira o passo a passo para começar a usar o mapa no Gemini: Deslize o carrossel de opções até encontrar “Mapa”; Permita que o Gemini acesse sua localização; Arraste o mapa e ajuste o zoom até encontrar a região desejada; Faça perguntas sobre o local ou peça sugestões de lugares para o Gemini. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ 16 comandos para usar o Gemini no Google Maps ”.

sources.title: Cómo usar Gemini para encontrar, analizar y comparar productos antes de comprarlos
sources.text: Aplicaciones como ChatGPT, Claude o Gemini se han convertido en imprescindibles para millones de personas que buscan responder sus preguntas , obtener una explicación sobre algo que no entienden o, simplemente, obtener mejores resultados al buscar por internet . Y si hablamos de búsquedas online, muchas de ellas tienen que ver con comprar un producto o contratar un servicio . De ahí que existan tantos comparadores de viajes, telefonía, compañías eléctricas, electrónica o videojuegos. Es más. Comprar con Gemini o ChatGPT cada vez está más cerca de convertirse en una experiencia todo en uno. Este año hemos visto cómo Google ha ido incorporando elementos relacionados con las compras en sus productos y servicios . Como el carrito universal , que todavía no está presente en todos los países o las constantes mejoras del modo IA de Google y de Gemini enfocadas, precisamente a comprar por internet directamente desde su asistente de inteligencia artificial. Además, ya hemos visto con anterioridad que combinando Gemini y la cámara de tu móvil puedes organizar mejor tus compras . En este artículo vamos a ver de qué manera es posible comprar con Gemini . O, mejor dicho, qué cosas puedes pedirle a la IA de Google para ayudarte durante todo el proceso previo a la compra en sí. Por ejemplo, comparar precios, modelos del mismo producto, encontrar aquello que necesitas, inspirarte si no sabes qué regalar… En definitiva, Gemini puede ser un buen aliado y un asistente de compras si sabes cómo usarlo en tu favor. Comprar con Gemini puede resultar muy cómodo si sabes explicarle bien lo que necesitas . Primero, ¿sabes ya qué vas a comprar? Entonces, pídele que busque la tienda más barata. Si no estás seguro, pregúntale qué producto es mejor entre dos o tres que tengas en mente. Y si no tienes idea de lo que necesitas exactamente, expon tus necesidades y Gemini te dará las soluciones más aproximadas. Aquí van varios ejemplos de prompts sobre compras para empezar: En resumen, al buscar algo en Gemini, deberías tener en cuenta : Gemini nos da una plantilla para hacer una búsqueda de este tipo: “Quiero comprar [producto] para [uso concreto]. Presupuesto: [cantidad]. Debe cumplir: [requisitos imprescindibles]. Prefiero evitar: [restricciones]. Busca opciones disponibles en España, compáralas en una tabla con precio, especificaciones, ventajas, inconvenientes, garantía y reseñas. Después, dame X finalistas, señala riesgos y dime qué comprobaría yo mismo antes de pagar.” Hay muchos parámetros que te hacen decidirte por un producto. Según lo que sea, tal vez te interese lo económico . En otros casos, buscarás que dure mucho y se rompa poco . Otros productos te interesarán más por si tiene piezas de sustitución o recargables baratos . Y, muchas veces, tal vez quieras conocer qué te conviene más si hay que elegir entre que sea bueno, bonito o barato. Así que procura decírselo cuando busques qué comprar con Gemini. Por ejemplo, si vas a comprar algo tan genérico como un teléfono móvil y no tienes un candidato concreto, puedes preguntarle a Gemini que te muestra las mejores opciones según diferentes parámetros : los de mejor calidad, los más económicos, los que mejor combinen calidad-precio… Así, la IA te los mostrará en grupos comparando todas las opciones y te será más fácil decidirte por uno u otro. Las tablas son un elemento visual muy práctico cuando no te decides por un modelo concreto de ese producto que quieres comprar. Si tienes cuatro o cinco opciones a elegir, una tabla te resolverá las dudas. Así que díselo a Gemini, indicando que incluya parámetros como precio final, características más destacadas, dimensiones, peso, garantía… Según qué estés buscando comprar, puedes pedir mil y una cosas que te decantarán por una u otra opción. Materiales de fabricación, opinión de los usuarios y de los expertos, si cumple con los estándares o normativas… No des por sentado que Gemini te va a proporcionar toda la información que necesitas. Especifícalo tú mismo para que la tabla resultante sea lo más completa posible. Cuanto más caro es lo que quieres comprar, más tiempo le dedicarás a la búsqueda . Con Gemini ocurre igual. Si se trata de comprar con Gemini algo que te supondrá un desembolso considerable de dinero, te conviene utilizar la función Deep Research . En castellano, investigación profunda. Le llevará más tiempo a la IA darte una respuesta. Pero esa respuesta será un informe más preciso sobre lo que estás buscando. Y merece la pena. Además, en el modo Deep Research de Gemini puedes incluir tus propias fuentes . Por ejemplo, buscando tus propias fuentes en Google o subiendo archivos de manuales, prospectos, catálogos o folletos de productos. Así te asegurarás de que la IA busque donde tú quieres y te dé la información acorde a fuentes que tú consideres fiables o de confianza. Dedícale tiempo a esto antes de lanzar tu pregunta a Gemini y obtendrás mejores respuestas . Otra manera de ayudarte a decidirte entre dos o tres productos similares consiste en ver qué dicen los demás. Aunque las reseñas y opiniones tienen sus más y sus menos, y a veces hay que cogerlas con pinzas, pueden servir de ayuda. Así que pídele a Gemini que te diga qué opiniones merecen en internet determinado producto y si hay quejas o polémicas . Esto sirve tanto para el producto o servicio como para la tienda o proveedor del servicio . Hay tiendas y comercios en los que confiamos a ciegas. Pero es posible que encuentres un nuevo sitio con buenos precios que quieras probar. Si no lo conoces, necesitarás opiniones favorables que te hagan confiar en él. O, al contrario, que te libren de una mala experiencia. Pregunta si la compra es segura , si el envío es correcto, si hay atención al cliente , sede física, si el servicio posterior a la compra es el adecuado… Toda precaución es poca cuando se trata de comprar. stories.title: How U Mobile built agentic telco operations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
stories.summary: U Mobile, Malaysia's newest 5G network provider, built AiDaH, an agentic AI operations platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that moves beyond AI assistance to autonomous action across telco operations. Nine months after production launch, AiDaH handles over 150 operational scenarios across six divisions, cutting trouble tickets by up to 84.5%.

sources.name: AWS Machine Learning
sources.title: How U Mobile built agentic telco operations with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sources.text: U Mobile, Malaysia’s newest 5G network provider, has always run its telco operations lean, doing more with less through continuous automation. When new AI capabilities became available, U Mobile explored how to enhance operational efficiency beyond basic productivity gains. The real opportunity was further upstream, in how operations teams diagnose and resolve problems in the first place. The same lean operating discipline shaped the foundation for AiDaH: not a one-off technology initiative, but the next step in a long-running journey to simplify operations and scale capability without adding complexity. When a subscriber can’t purchase a data add-on, resolving it isn’t a single problem. It’s a coordination problem. A customer service agent needs to pull interface logs for error codes. The same agent must then query business support system APIs for subscriber eligibility, and cross-reference internal knowledge bases for applicable business policies. All of that happens across multiple systems, before drafting a single word of response. And when that fails, the ticket escalates to backend IT teams and the subscriber waits even longer. Traditional automation tools can help agents write better responses. What they can’t do is navigate multiple systems, analyze the results, and propose corrective action. Closing that gap takes an agentic architecture built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. U Mobile’s Information Systems Division (ISD) built exactly that. Working with AWS and AWS Partner Axrail, they created AiDaH, the AI-Driven Agentic Helpdesk, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. Two capabilities decided the choice. The managed agent runtime meant there was no agent infrastructure to operate. Built-in memory carried conversational context across turns without standing up a separate state store. Within a year of starting the journey, AiDaH handles over 150 documented operational scenarios across six business divisions. U Mobile’s internal measurements show trouble ticket volumes falling by up to 84.5 percent in key categories. In this post, we walk through the six-layer architecture behind AiDaH. We then describe the security foundation beneath the platform, and close with a brief note on the spec-driven method the team used to build it. U Mobile’s IT landscape reflects the complexity typical of modern telecommunications: business support and customer relationship management systems, mobile number portability platforms, big data analytics, and infrastructure monitoring tools, running hybrid across on-premises and cloud. Before AiDaH, this fragmentation meant that even routine diagnoses required manually checking logs, querying subscriber eligibility, and consulting knowledge bases for business policies, across separate systems and portals. Each lookup was a context switch, each context switch was time lost, and each unresolved query became an escalation to a backend IT team. Expanding coverage to additional operational domains compounded the problem, because every new system typically required a bespoke integration. The ISD team’s strategy rested on three pillars. AiDaH started with a principle: think big, start small. U Mobile began conceptualization in late 2025 with two pilot agents and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, a fully managed Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) capability. A Q1 2026 pilot brought the internal IT helpdesk online with 4 agents and 20 operational scenarios. Through 2026 the platform hardened and expanded, adding three-tier routing and reaching 6 agents by mid-year. AiDaH went live to 50 L2 call center and branch users in Q3 2026 with 8 agents, and now covers more than 150 documented operational scenarios. The difference between traditional AI assistance and agentic AI is best illustrated through a real example. With a traditional AI assistant, a support agent handling “mobile data not working overseas” gets help drafting a response and some suggested troubleshooting steps, but still manually checks roaming status, verifies eligibility, raises tickets, and sends the final reply. With AiDaH, the system independently checks the subscriber’s roaming configuration, verifies international data eligibility, and identifies the specific point of failure. It then assembles a remediation plan: which services to reset, what configuration to push, and whether a network ticket is warranted. The support agent reviews and confirms, and the actions execute. The investigation that used to consume the agent’s time now happens before they read the first line. The human decision point is preserved where it matters: at the moment something changes on a live subscriber account. In one production case, a subscriber reported being unable to purchase an add-on. AiDaH traced the failure to an error code, “Subscriber has pending order.” It also revealed that the customer had attempted the same purchase more than 30 times across multiple channels over three days, every attempt blocked by the same underlying pending order. AiDaH surfaced the root cause and the remediation steps in a single response. Previously that would have required manual investigation across several systems. AiDaH runs on a layered architecture built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, deployed in the Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region. Staff interact through Microsoft Teams, a deliberate choice to meet most users where they already work, with no new application to learn and no portal switching. The following diagram shows how the layers fit together. As shown in Figure 1, the platform is organized into six layers. Staff reach AiDaH through Microsoft Teams and a web portal served by Amazon CloudFront and protected by AWS WAF, with an AWS Lambda backend and a REST API for programmatic triggers. sources.title: How Greenlight Financial built an autonomous SOC solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
sources.text: Greenlight Financial resolves more than 90 percent of up to 4,000 security and risk cases each month without human intervention. Greenlight’s Luna uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore , infrastructure for building, connecting, and optimizing agents at scale. Specifically, Greenlight uses AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to host Luna’s agent code. It uses AgentCore memory, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, to support its tiered multi-agent system. This avoids the need to build and operate these capabilities in-house. Luna triages dark web breach-card alerts, identity anomalies, and financial-risk events in seconds. This post explains how Greenlight Financial built an autonomous security operations center (SOC) solution on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover its multi-tiered supervisor architecture, more than 30 specialized agents, episodic memory for continuous learning, and expansion from SOC use cases into financial risk triage. We share production metrics, infrastructure decisions, and patterns for building autonomous security operations in regulated industries. Greenlight Financial provides financial products for families: debit cards, savings tools, and connected devices such as the Family Hub and Pet Tracker. The company processes sensitive financial data at scale under the same regulatory requirements as major banks. Greenlight’s SOC receives 3,000–4,000 security and risk alerts per month from four primary vectors: Each alert demands cross-referencing multiple data sources before an analyst can render a verdict. A single dark web breach card notification requires checking whether the card is active, deduplicating against prior notifications, reviewing customer session data, and checking open support tickets. This workflow takes a human analyst 15-30 minutes per case. At 4,000 cases per month, that math breaks. Greenlight built Luna as a hierarchical multi-agent system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The architecture follows a tiered supervisor pattern that mirrors how human SOC teams operate. L1 handles volume, and L2 handles complexity. Figure 1: Luna’s tiered supervisor architecture on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Tier 1 supervisor uses an advanced language model available through Amazon Bedrock running on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime within an Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC). The runtime uses private subnets and direct code deployment through a ZIP file and Amazon Simple Storage Service ( Amazon S3 ). It handles initial triage of incoming cases by orchestrating more than 30 specialized agents: The Tier 1 supervisor receives cases through two paths: Amazon API Gateway, which exposes the Luna Queue API and a Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint, and Tines SOAR for automated alert ingestion. It determines which specialized agents to invoke based on alert type, synthesizes their findings, and renders a verdict. The median triage time for routine cases is single-digit seconds. Cases that exceed Tier 1’s confidence threshold escalate to a Tier 2 supervisor using an advanced foundation model on Amazon Bedrock with extended reasoning capabilities. This agent handles the 10 percent of cases that require multi-step reasoning: The Tier 2 supervisor runs on a scheduled basis, using Amazon EventBridge rate triggers and Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) queue completions to batch-process escalated cases, and on demand for urgent Tier 1-escalated cases. Different teams engage Luna in different ways, so the application exposes three entry points. These range from fully automated alert ingestion to interactive, on-demand investigation. Each entry point maps to a persona and how their work arrives: The memory layer is built on AgentCore memory. This layer is what separates Luna from a stateless triage tool. It supports pattern recognition, deduplication, and continuous accuracy improvement. Stores recent events and resolution outcomes. When a new alert arrives, Luna checks: “Have I seen this pattern in the last 30 days? What was the verdict? Is this a known behavior that I should allowlist?” Concrete example: A Greenlight infrastructure role generates a specific access pattern every Tuesday at 3 AM for scheduled maintenance.
